index.title: Hushpad — The quiet, private notepad for Windows and Mac
index.description: A free, open-source notepad for Windows and Mac that saves as you type, encrypts every note, and stays out of screenshots and screen sharing. Passwords, API keys, HTML, JSON and screenshots, all in one place.
index.ogDescription: Auto-save · Every note encrypted · A window screenshots can't see. A free, open-source notepad for Windows and Mac.
index.lead: What you type is saved as you go, no save button needed. Every note is encrypted and kept in one folder, and the window never shows up in screenshots or screen shares. Passwords, API keys, HTML, JSON and screenshots, all in one place.

index.shotDarkAlt: Hushpad in dark mode — a code note with color-highlighted JSON

pains.h2: If this is how you use Notepad
pains.p: Tabs that stick around without saving are handy, until they start piling up.
pains.q1: “Too many tabs, and they all look alike”
pains.a1: Sort things out with the note list, folders and search, and each tab shows when the note was created. A single click opens a preview tab, so browsing around doesn't leave a trail of new tabs.
pains.q2: “I worry everything's gone if my PC shuts down”
pains.a2: Your text is safely written to disk as you type, and a previous version is kept every 10 minutes. Even if the power cuts out mid-save, your latest text is intact.
pains.q3: “I keep passwords and API keys in Notepad”
pains.a3: Every note is stored only as an encrypted file. Secret notes are masked each time you open them, and anything you copy from them is cleared from the clipboard after 30 seconds.

feat.h2: Lightweight, with just what you need
feat.p: Start typing right away, just like Windows Notepad, while Hushpad quietly handles what Notepad never could.

save.p: Saved the moment you type. No need to name anything: notes are sorted by the date and time they were created, all in one folder.

lock.p: Open the files and there's nothing to read. Other apps, search indexers and cloud services can't see what's inside.

hide.p: Screenshots, screen recordings and screen sharing in video calls don't pick up the Hushpad window. Only you can see it.

copy.p: Paste formatted text from the web as is, then copy it out as plain text with <kbd>Ctrl+Shift+C</kbd>. Rich notes always keep a plain-text version alongside.

code.p: Code notes come with line numbers, syntax colors and auto-indent, plus one-step JSON formatting. On a KEY=value line, copy just the value.

shot.p: From anywhere, press <kbd>Ctrl+Alt+S</kbd> to capture an area or <kbd>Ctrl+Alt+R</kbd> to record the screen. Results land straight in a note, and videos are encrypted too.

folder.p: Drag notes into folders, merge several into one, and restore deleted notes from the trash. You can even round up notes you haven't opened in a while and tidy them away.

sync.p: Keep your vault folder in Dropbox or OneDrive and open it on another PC with the same password. One note is one file, so conflicts are rare.

search.p: Search note titles, note contents and every command from one box, then press Enter to run it. <kbd>Ctrl+Alt+M</kbd> saves your clipboard straight to a new note.

capture.h2: On your screen. Not in the capture.
capture.p: Keep a note open while you share your screen, or take a screenshot: wherever the Hushpad window sits, the capture shows what's behind it. So go ahead and capture without moving the window out of the way.
capture.b1: Screenshot and recording tools, video-call sharing
capture.s1: On Windows it uses the capture exclusion built into the system (Windows 10 version 2004 or later). On macOS it turns off sharing for the window.
capture.b2: Recording controls stay out of the shot
capture.s2: The recording frame and the ⏸ ⏹ bar appear only on your screen.
capture.b3: Turn it off when you need to
capture.s3: When you do want to show a note on a screen share, one click in the menu turns it off.

sec.p: Hushpad has no server. Your notes live only in the folder you choose, and every file in it is encrypted.
sec.s1: Notes, previous versions, videos, even folder names: everything is stored encrypted. Only while a recording is in progress does a temporary file exist, and it is deleted when the recording ends.
sec.b2: A key derived from your password (scrypt)
sec.s2: Without the password, the files can't be decrypted. If you forget it, not even the developer can recover them.
sec.b3: Enter it once on your own PC
sec.s3: Hushpad remembers the key through your Windows account (DPAPI) or your macOS login keychain. On another account or another computer, you'll need the password again.
sec.s4: Copied text is flagged to stay out of Windows clipboard history and cloud clipboard sync.
sec.b5: No account, no tracking, no internet
sec.s5: Neither the app nor this website uses analytics or ad scripts.

keys.p: Some shortcuts work even while the window is closed to the tray (the menu bar on a Mac). On a Mac, press ⌃⌥ (Control+Option) instead of Ctrl+Alt, and ⌘ instead of Ctrl inside the app.
keys.k2: Save the clipboard as a note

items.a: From this site's download page. Files are published on GitHub Releases in two builds: one for Windows 10 and 11 (64-bit) and one for Macs with Apple silicon (M1 or later). Intel-based Macs are not supported.

items.q: Is it free? Is it open source?
items.a: Yes to both. Hushpad is free, and its source code is published on GitHub under GPL-3.0-or-later. Anyone can read, change and redistribute it. If you distribute a modified version, you need to publish its source under the same license and give it a different name and icon.

items.q: Can I bring over the tabs I have open in Windows Notepad?
items.a: Yes. On Windows, Menu › File › Import Windows Notepad tabs copies them over, unsaved tabs included, and leaves Windows Notepad untouched.

items.q: What if I forget my password?
items.a: There's no way to recover it. Hushpad is built so that no one, not even its developer, can open your notes without the password. Write it down somewhere safe when you first set it.

items.q: Are my notes still there after a restart?
items.a: Yes. Notes are encrypted and written to disk as you type, so they're there when your computer comes back on. After the first run, Hushpad starts in the tray when Windows starts (on a Mac, in the menu bar when you log in). If you'd rather it didn't, turn this off from the tray icon's menu or the Security menu.

items.q: How do I use it on more than one PC?
items.a: Keep your vault folder inside a synced folder such as Dropbox or OneDrive, then choose the same folder on your other PC and enter the same password. Changes made on another PC show up within seconds, and if both sides edit at the same time, one version is kept separately as a “conflict copy.”

items.q: Can I add images or videos?
items.a: You can paste or drag images into rich-text notes, and screenshots and short screen recordings (up to 3 minutes) go straight in. Videos play inside the app and are stored encrypted.

items.q: Does it send anything over the internet?
items.a: No. Hushpad has no account and no server, and it doesn't connect to the internet while it runs.

items.q: Is it hidden from capture on a Mac, too?
items.a: On macOS, Hushpad turns off sharing for its window. On macOS 15 and later, though, some capture and screen-sharing apps that use ScreenCaptureKit ignore that setting and can still capture the window. On a Mac, check for yourself before you share your screen.

items.q: Can I change the app's language?
items.a: The app comes in Korean, English, Japanese and Simplified Chinese, and starts in your system language. You can switch anytime under Menu (⋯) › View › Language.

dl.title: Download — Hushpad
dl.description: Download Hushpad free for Windows 10 and 11 (64-bit) and for Macs with Apple silicon. First-run steps, system requirements and file verification (SHA-256).
dl.notice: We're getting the release version ready. Once it's out, you can download it right here, at this same address.
dl.uiNote: The app comes in Korean, English, Japanese and Simplified Chinese, and starts in your system language. Switch anytime under Menu (⋯) › View › Language.

first: Download the zip file and extract it wherever you like (your Documents folder, for example). There's no installer.
Open the extracted Hushpad folder and run Hushpad.exe.

If “Windows protected your PC” appears, click “More info › Run anyway.” Hushpad isn't code-signed yet, so SmartScreen may warn you about it. If you'd like to be sure first, check the SHA-256 value as described below.
Choose a folder for your notes and set a password. To use Hushpad on several PCs, pick a folder inside Dropbox or OneDrive.

mac.req: Macs with Apple silicon (M1 or later)
first: Download and unzip the file, then move Hushpad.app to your Applications folder.

The first time, right-click (or Control-click) Hushpad.app in Finder, choose “Open,” then click “Open” again in the warning. The app isn't signed or notarized by Apple, so double-clicking won't open it. If you don't see an Open button, go to System Settings › Privacy & Security and click “Open Anyway.”

The first time you take a screenshot or record your screen, macOS asks for Screen Recording permission. Turn on Hushpad under System Settings › Privacy & Security › Screen & System Audio Recording (Screen Recording on macOS 14 and earlier), then restart the app.
Choose a folder for your notes and set a password. The system-wide shortcuts are ⌃⌥N (new note), ⌃⌥M (clipboard to note), ⌃⌥S (screenshot) and ⌃⌥R (screen recording).

auto.p: After the first run, Hushpad starts in the tray when Windows starts (on a Mac, in the menu bar when you log in). Notes are encrypted and saved as you type, so they're still there after a restart. You can turn auto-start off from the tray or menu bar icon's menu, or from the Security menu.

items: Windows: Windows 10 (version 2004 or later) or Windows 11, 64-bit. Hiding the window from capture needs Windows 10 version 2004 or later.
Mac: a Mac with Apple silicon (M1 or later). There is no build for Intel-based Macs.

hash.p: Compare your download with the SHA-256 value shown above. On Windows, run Get-FileHash .\Hushpad-win64.zip in PowerShell. On a Mac, run shasum -a 256 Hushpad-macos-arm64.zip in Terminal.

remove.p: If auto-start is on, turn it off from the tray or menu bar icon first, then delete the program folder (Hushpad.app on a Mac). Your notes stay in the vault folder, still encrypted. To remove the notes as well, delete the vault folder too.
